title: Troubleshooting: Why Your Herb Scissors Leave Uneven Pieces
meta_description: Learn how to fix uneven cuts from herb scissors and keep your greens finely minced every time. Get practical tips, troubleshooting steps, and a review of the He
html:
When you’re chopping fresh cilantro, basil, or chives with a pair of herb scissors, you expect a uniform, fine mince that blends effortlessly into sauces, salsas, and salads. But if your cuts feel lumpy or uneven, you’re probably dealing with herb scissors uneven pieces troubleshooting issues. Below, I break down common causes and offer straightforward fixes so you can get that perfect, even mincing every time.

1. Blade Wear and Alignment

The most frequent culprit is worn or misaligned blades. Even a small nick can cause a blade to bite unevenly, leaving some leaves chopped finely while others stay chunky. Check each of the five blades for:

  • Sharpness – A dull edge will drag leaves instead of slicing cleanly.
  • Alignment – If a blade is bent or out of line with the others, it will cut at a different angle.
  • Any nicks or chips that could snag leaves.

If you notice any of these, it’s time to replace the scissors or have them professionally sharpened. The Herb Scissors are made with a durable steel that resists nicking, but even they can benefit from a quick sharpening session every few months.

2. Incorrect Stacking Technique

Herb scissors rely on a simple stacking method: place the leaves on the top blade, close the scissors, and snip. A common mistake is stacking leaves too high or too low relative to the blade’s cutting line. This misalignment can create uneven mincing because the blades don’t cut all leaves at the same depth.

Try these steps:

  1. Lay a single layer of herbs, roughly the thickness of the blade gap.
  2. Press gently with your thumb to keep the leaves flat.
  3. Close the scissors fully—if you feel resistance, open slightly and re‑stack.
  4. Snap once; repeat until all leaves are minced.

Practice will make the technique feel natural, and you’ll notice a consistent texture.

3. Inadequate Cleaning and Maintenance

Residual plant matter can clog the blade gaps, especially after multiple uses. If the blades are clogged, they won’t slice cleanly, resulting in uneven pieces. The Herb Scissors come with a built‑in cleaning comb that’s designed to pull out debris from each blade channel.

After each use:

  • Wipe the blades with a damp cloth.
  • Use the cleaning comb to remove stuck leaves.
  • Dry the scissors thoroughly to prevent rust.

Neglecting this simple step is a quick way to create uneven mincing.

4. The Role of Herb Texture and Moisture

Some herbs, like basil, are naturally tender and moist, while others, like cilantro, are tougher. When you try to mince a mix of textures in one batch, the scissors may struggle with the tougher leaves, leaving them less finely chopped.

To avoid this:

  • Separate herbs by texture before mincing.
  • For moist herbs, pat them dry with a towel to reduce slippage.
  • Use a slightly lighter force on tougher leaves to prevent the blades from getting stuck.

5. Using the Right Amount of Force

Applying too much pressure can bend the blades or cause them to clamp too tightly, leading to uneven cuts. Conversely, too little pressure won’t engage all five blades fully. Find the sweet spot by:

  1. Gripping the handle firmly but not rigidly.
  2. Snapping the scissors with a quick, decisive motion.
  3. Releasing the pressure after each snip to let the blades reset.

Consistency in force translates to consistent mincing.

6. When to Replace Your Herb Scissors

Even with diligent care, every cutting tool has a lifespan. Look for signs that it’s time for a new pair:

  • Blades that no longer stay aligned.
  • Visible rust or corrosion.
  • Difficulty opening the scissors after a clean.

The Herb Scissors are engineered for durability, but if they can’t meet your mincing standards, it’s time to upgrade.

FAQ

Why does my herb scissors keep leaving some leaves chunky?

Check blade sharpness and alignment first. Dull or misaligned blades will cut unevenly. Also, ensure you’re stacking the herbs correctly and using the cleaning comb after each use.

Can I use my herb scissors on herbs with stems, like cilantro?

Yes, but first trim the stems to a uniform length. Stems are tougher and can cause uneven cuts if left too long. Trim them to about a half‑inch and then mince.

Is it necessary to clean my herb scissors after every use?

Cleaning after every use prevents debris buildup that can clog the blades. A quick wipe and a pass through the cleaning comb will keep your scissors in top shape and ensure even mincing.
